title: 2026 Session Priorities: Comprehensive reform package will improve program integrity, from program design to post-payment analytics
notes: This is a legislative-session budget PRIORITIES/PROPOSAL document dated 04/2026 describing measures in Governor Tim Walz's 2026 supplemental budget -- it is DHS advocating for these reforms to the legislature, not a record that they have all already been enacted or implemented. Several items described (a new statewide Office of Inspector General, codifying HSS termination in statute, several billing-rule and rate-methodology changes) are proposals, not yet-adopted law, as of this document's own text. Do not cite this PDF as proof that any specific proposed measure is already in effect; separately verify enactment (e.g. via session law) before upgrading a proposal to an implemented fact. supports: DHS describes a comprehensive program-integrity reform package proposed in Governor Tim Walz's 2026 supplemental budget, covering the Medicaid program lifecycle from program design through provider enrollment, prepayment review, payment controls, and post-payment data analytics.
Proposals include a data-driven preenrollment risk assessment process, enhanced revalidation processes, and stricter background-studies requirements for high-risk providers.

The proposal includes a statutory update to codify the termination of the Housing Stabilization Services program and directs DHS to develop recommendations for a redesigned housing services benefit, with a stated deadline of September 15, 2027.

The proposal includes establishing a new statewide Office of Inspector General to investigate and prevent fraud and misuse of public funds across state programs, with investigation and data-research teams and a case management system.

The proposal would cap administrative fees at 6% for certain disability-waiver and older-adult programs (Alternative Care, Essential Community Supports, Elderly Waiver), citing the current lack of such a limit as allowing some providers to bill the maximum allowable rate regardless of actual cost.

The proposal includes new reforms specific to Integrated Community Supports, including a 15-minute billing unit, acuity-aligned rate limits, distinct funding streams for housing versus waiver services, and a license moratorium for new providers.
does_not_support: That any of these proposals have been enacted into law or fully implemented; this document is DHS's session-priorities advocacy document, dated April 2026, describing what the department is asking the legislature to fund and authorize.
